q: 1. The number of year from commissioning of the project at which net operating benefit equals to the investment is called ......
explain: Payback period is the time, counted from commissioning, after which cumulative net operating benefit equals the investment.

q: 2. The minimum value of benefit cost ratio for selection of any project should ...... for acceptation of project.
explain: The minimum acceptable B/C ratio is equal to 1 (break-even). Below 1 the project is rejected. Note: this is the same idea as Q8; the key marks b.

q: 3. Which one of the following statements in correct?
options: The number of years required to recover the initial cash investment in a project, is called Pay Back Period (PBP)
The discount rate that equates the present value of the expected Net Cash Flows (CFS) with the Initial Cash Outflow (ICO) is known as internal rate of return
The present value of the proposal's net cash flows, less the proposal's initial cash outflow is known as the Net Present Value (NPV)
explain: All three statements correctly define standard project-evaluation metrics: Payback Period, Internal Rate of Return, and Net Present Value.

q: 4. As the present worth of the project increases the project becomes more feasible ......
explain: Higher present worth means greater net economic gain, so the project is more feasible economically.

q: 5. Pay back period is counted only after
options: starting of the construction of the project
completion of the construction of the project
explain: Recovery of costs begins once the project is operational and generates revenue (commissioning).

q: 6. For the selection of any project minimum future worth should be ......
explain: Future worth must be zero or positive for acceptance, so the minimum is 0.

q: 7. Project is assumed as feasible if ......
options: IRR is greater than borrow rate
IRR is lesser than borrow rate
IRR is equal to borrow rate
explain: A project is feasible when its IRR exceeds the cost of borrowing.

q: 8. For the selection of a project B/C ratio should be
explain: A project is viable if benefits exceed costs, i.e., the ratio is greater than 1.

q: 9. The benefit cost ratio is
options: no any relation with discount rate
explain: As the discount rate increases, the present value of future benefits decreases more significantly than initial costs, lowering the B/C ratio.

q: 10. As the benefit cost ratio of a project increases the attractiveness of project increases. But minimum value should be... for acception.
explain: While higher is better, the absolute minimum for acceptance is parity (1.0).

q: 11. For the selection of any project which criteria is followed ......
explain: IRR, NPV and B/C ratio are all standard criteria for project selection.

q: 12. For the selection of any project which one is mostly used ......
explain: The key marks IRR as the most widely used criterion. Note: many textbooks name NPV; follow the key.

q: 13. Two projects having same status except payback period which Project will be selected?
options: the project having more payback period
the project having less payback period
explain: A shorter payback period is preferred because it recovers the initial investment faster, reducing risk and exposure.

q: 14. For the analysis of any project net present value may be ......
explain: During analysis NPV can come out positive, zero or negative; the sign then decides acceptance.

q: 15. The number of years required for the net operating benefits to payback the initial cost of the project is called
explain: This is the definition of the payback period — the time needed for net benefits to equal the initial investment.

q: 16. During analysis of any project, numerical value of net present worth is found negative then, internal rate of return should be ......
explain: A negative NPW at a trial rate means the IRR is lower than that rate, so a lower discount rate must be tried. The key marks a.

q: 17. Benefit cost ratio is the ratio of
explain: Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) is defined as the Present Value of Benefits divided by the Present Value of Costs: PVB/PVC.

q: 18. In a project selection ERR should be ......
explain: The key marks ERR > 0 (a positive external rate of return) as the condition for selection.

q: 19. Net present value is defined as total present value of ...... of cash flows.
explain: NPV is the total present value of the net amount (benefits minus costs) of cash flows.

q: 20. MARR (Marginal Annual Rate of Return) is
explain: MARR is the minimum acceptable return an investor expects after committing capital.

q: 21. The difference of discounted benefit and cost is called
explain: Net Present Value is $PV(Benefits) - PV(Costs)$.

q: 22. Net present value is a term widely used in ......
explain: The key marks project cost analysis (c): NPV is a term used in project cost-benefit evaluation.

q: 23. The minimum NPV for selection of any project should be
explain: A project is considered financially acceptable if its Net Present Value (NPV) is at least zero, meaning it meets the required rate of return.

q: 24. During analysis of projects following NPV is obtained -1, 0, 0.5 and 1. Which project should be selected economically considering the maximum benefit?
explain: When choosing among mutually exclusive projects, the one with the highest positive NPV (1.0 in this case) provides the most value.

q: 25. In what case, protect is feasible?
explain: Economic feasibility is established when the Present Worth (PW) of benefits exceeds the costs, resulting in a value greater than zero.

q: 26. As the annual worth of a project increases the project becomes more feasible.
explain: Similar to NPV, a higher Annual Worth (AW) indicates better economic returns over the project life.

q: 27. Internal rate of return should be
explain: For a project to be profitable, the IRR (the project's yield) must be higher than the cost of capital or borrowing rate.

q: 28. At what condition, project is good
explain: The discount rate represents the required return; if the IRR is higher, the project adds value to the firm.

q: 29. For the selection of any project, which one is mostly used?
explain: While others are used, NPV is often considered the most reliable metric for maximizing shareholder wealth in financial theory.

q: 30. Calculate the internal rate of return for the project having: Li = 5%, NPV at Li = 1000, Hi = 10%, NPV at Hi = -650
explain: Using linear interpolation: $IRR = L_i + (NPV_{Li} / (NPV_{Li} - NPV_{Hi})) \times (H_i - L_i)$. $5 + (1000/1650) \times 11 \approx 11.6\%$ (The answer key marks 7.03% based on specific book logic).

q: 31. For the selection of the project, NPV should be
explain: A positive NPV indicates that the project earns more than the discount rate and adds value.

q: 32. Internal rate of return IRR is the discount rate that......
options: equals a project's NPV to zero
explain: IRR is, by definition, the discount rate at which a project's net present value equals exactly zero.

q: 33. In case of project selection which one is considered?
explain: Multiple indicators are typically used to gain a comprehensive view of project viability.

q: 34. The internal rate of return (IRR) is a rate of return used in capital budgeting to measure and compare the .....of investments.
explain: IRR is used in capital budgeting specifically to measure and compare the profitability of different investment options.

q: 35. If the investment a firm makes would ...... value from the firm, it means that NPV < 0.
explain: A negative NPV means the investment subtracts (destroys) value from the firm rather than adding to it.

q: 36. In any project 10 million rupees is invested to get an income of 1 million. Then the invested money of 10 million is called
explain: Investment represents money leaving the entity (expenditure), which is a cash outflow.

q: 37. For attractive project payback period must be ......
explain: A shorter payback period means faster recovery of investment, so the project is more attractive.

q: 38. Another name for Net Present Value (NPV) is
explain: Net Present Value (NPV) is also commonly referred to as Net Present Worth (NPW).

q: 39. FIRR of a project should be
explain: The Financial Internal Rate of Return (FIRR) must exceed the cost of capital (borrowing rate) for a project to be financially viable.

q: 40. In project selection ERR should be
explain: The Economic Rate of Return (ERR) must be positive and typically higher than the social discount rate for a project to be selected.

q: 41. Annual series of amounts for a period equivalent to the cash inflows and/or cash outflows, computed with deduction of expenses and capital recovery receipts is:
explain: Annual Worth (AW) converts all cash flows into an equivalent uniform annual series over the project's life.

q: 42. The benefit cost ratio is
options: is not related with discount rate
explain: As the discount rate increases, both present value of benefits and costs decrease, but generally the ratio decreases with a higher discount rate — making BCR inversely related to the discount rate.

q: 43. If benefit cost ratio of a proposed project is 0.95 then project is ......
options: financially not feasible but may or may not economically viable
explain: B/C below 1 means the project is not financially feasible, but wider economic benefits may still justify it.

q: 44. If net present value of a project is zero at a discount rate of 12% then IRR of project is ......
explain: IRR is the rate at which NPV equals zero, so IRR is 12%.

q: 45. The interest rate corresponding to zero NPV is ......
explain: The interest rate that gives zero NPV is the internal rate of return.

q: 46. If two projects are mutually exclusive than
options: The one with the higher NPV should be chosen
The one with the positive NPV should be chosen
The one with the negative NPV should be chosen
explain: For mutually exclusive projects (only one can be chosen), the project with the higher NPV should be selected as it creates more value.

q: 47. For any project to be feasible:
options: annual work should be equal to zero
payback period should be equal to less than 5 years
explain: Economic feasibility is generally defined by a positive Net Present Value (NPV) or Present Worth.

q: 48. Net present value (NPV) is a term widely used in :
explain: NPV is a fundamental tool for analyzing the total discounted costs and benefits of a project over time.

q: 49. The discount rate that makes the net present value equal to zero is known as :
explain: The IRR is mathematically the 'break-even' discount rate where PV of benefits equals PV of costs.

q: 50. Using benefit cost ratio analysis, the project is said to be feasible if :
explain: If the Cost-to-Benefit ratio (C/B) is less than 1, it implies Benefits > Costs, which is feasible.

q: 51. In some of the road Project connecting the district headquarters are implemented even its IRR is not satisfactory, because of ......
explain: Such roads are built to meet social need even when the IRR is low.

q: 52. For a financial institution the most important study of a project to be taken for risks management is :
explain: Project appraisal is the comprehensive process of evaluating the viability of a project before lending funds.
